per_view.notes: Overly long blunt-ended grey tube; no nose taper or upswept tail cone. Front hump present with cockpit dots. Wing is a thin edge-on sliver; two crude box nacelles under belly. No vertical fin, only a needle-thin diagonal line at rear. Nose wheel plus clustered ball wheels on thin struts. Monochrome grey, square oversized windows.

Slender gray tube with front partial-length hump bearing upper-deck windows and a main-deck window row. No vertical stabilizer visible; only a thin flat plate at the tail. Two boxy block nacelles under the edge-on wing plate. Nose gear plus a small cluster of tiny main wheels. Blunt tail cone, uniform flat gray, thin floating antenna line.

Slender constant-width tube with rounded nose, blunt tail, dashed window rows, and a front oval hump region. Wings render only as hairline swept wires with no chord area; four nacelles float along them on tiny pylons. Empennage is thin edge lines. Two detached truck-like gear shapes beside fuselage. Planform does not read as a 747.

Slender grey tube with a consistent square window row, but the nose is a flat blunt disc. Wings are wire-thin rods with no chord or surface; empennage is bent sticks. Three nacelle cylinders visible, one floating above the fuselage on a rod. Tiny sphere blobs suggest gear. No distinct 747 hump; reads as a skeletal generic airliner.

Slender tube with good front hump, upper-deck and main-deck window rows, dark cockpit. Rear ends in a flat blunt disc, no tail cone. Wings are paper-thin swept sticks; four cylinder nacelles float detached near, not under, the wings. Tail surfaces are crude thin slabs with no tall fin. Small wheels sit loosely under mid-fuselage.

Slender tube ends in a flat blunt disc nose with a dark half-cylinder stuck on top instead of an ogive. Hump is a partial-length front shell with its own window row but visibly unblended. Thin slab wings; nacelles hang on stick pylons, some appearing detached. Tiny floating wheels; window line is consistent; uniform grey monochrome.

critic.fix_suggestion: Improve 'Empennage (tall vertical stabilizer + horizontal stabilizers)' (mean 3.43/10). Target the 8 anchor: single tall swept vertical stabilizer plus swept horizontal stabilizers at the tail cone, plausible sizes; then the 10 anchor: correct 747 empennage: very tall swept fin, low-mounted swept tailplane pair with dihedral, all tapered and proportioned to the fuselage.
